title: Lumbar FSU nucleus pressure sensitivity to axial compression (fibre-Bragg grating sensor)

quantity.name: IDP-load slope
quantity.definition: slope of nucleus pressure (FBG, centre of nucleus) vs axial compressive force, per specimen (mean±SD of the regression across repeats)

source.authors: Dennison CR, Wild PM, Byrnes PWG, Saari A, Itshayek E, Wilson DC, Zhu QA, Dvorak MFS, Cripton PA, Wilson DR
source.n: 5 specimens (5 lumbar FSUs: 3 L4-L5, 1 L2-L3, 1 L1-L2)
source.sample: human cadaver lumbar two-vertebra FSUs, Thompson/Galante grade 2-3

protocol.summary: Pure axial compression of lumbar FSUs in a materials testing machine (Instron 8874) 0 -> 2000 N -> 0 at 10 N/s after preconditioning cycles 0-2000 N at 200 N/s; ends potted in dental cement; loads visually checked as purely compressive. IDP sensors in the centre of the nucleus: FBG (10 mm active length, 125 um fibre via 25 G needle) or two needle-mounted strain-gauge sensors (2.45 mm diameter, Precision Measurement 060S). Pressure referenced to zero at 200 N (Fig 3 caption) - slopes only.
how_to_simulate: Model the FSU with both endplates fully bonded to rigid plates; constrain to pure axial compression.
Report slope of nucleus (centre) pressure vs compressive force (kPa/N) over the linear range; compare per level/specimen.
protocol.notes: Table 1 also gives disc grade (2-3) and major disc diameter 51-63 mm. Abstract prints L1-L2 FBG sensitivity as 0.702±0.043 kPa/N but Table 1 gives 0.705±0.043; Table value used (mean 0.902 kPa/N in text matches Table values).

extraction.check_notes: All 5 values, SDs, r2 re-read from Table 1; mean of five = 0.903 vs text 0.902 kPa/N.

pass_rule.rule: model slope within [min,max] of specimens of the same level (L4-L5: 0.847-1.07 kPa/N)
